IIHF games: schedules, shot locations, goals and penalties

Source: R/iihf.R
iihf.Rd

The IIHF's live-data feed (realtime.iihf.com, the one behind the game centre on iihf.com) has every game of its championships: the World Championship, the World Juniors, the women's and under-18 Worlds and the division tournaments, and the 2026 Olympics. For each game it has the score by period, the team stats, every goal with its scorer, assists and strength, every penalty and goalie change, and every shot with a place on the ice: goals, saves, blocked shots and shots that missed the net. Shot locations go back to the 2019 tournaments; older games have the rest.

Usage

iihf_schedule(year, event = "wm")

iihf_olympic_games()

iihf_game(game_id)

iihf_period_stats(game_id)

iihf_shots(game_id, length = 200, width = 85)

iihf_events(game_id)

Arguments

year

Year the tournament was played (the World Juniors that ran from December 2025 into January 2026 are 2026).

event

The tournament's code in iihf.com addresses: "wm" World Championship, "wm20" World Juniors, "ww" Women's World Championship, "wm18" and "ww18" the under-18s, and the divisions ("wm20ia", "wmia", ...).

game_id

IIHF game id, from iihf_schedule() or iihf_olympic_games(); the 2026 Olympic gold medal game is 1010000058.

length, width

Rink length and width in feet, for x and y.

Value

A tibble.

Details

  • iihf_schedule(): a tournament's games, with the ids the others take.

  • iihf_olympic_games(): every game of the 2026 Olympics, men's and women's (the Olympics are not on the IIHF's schedule pages).

  • iihf_game(): one game in a row: teams, final score, venue, date, attendance and how it ended.

  • iihf_period_stats(): shots on goal, saves, penalty minutes, power-play time and goals and faceoffs won, for each team in each period.

  • iihf_shots(): every shot, its result, who took it, and where.

  • iihf_events(): goals, penalties and goalie changes in order.

Where shots are. The feed places each shot on a 0-1 scale of the rink (x_raw along it, y_raw across). x and y scale that to feet from centre ice on a rink length by width (an NHL rink by default, which is what the 2026 Olympics used; IIHF rinks can be up to 60 m by 30 m), the frame nhl_rink() draws. Teams change ends between periods, so x_fixed and y_fixed turn every shot so its team attacks to the right (each team's direction in a period is the end most of its shots were taken at), and distance (feet) and angle (degrees off the middle) are measured to the net it attacked. The table works with plot_shots().

Shot results are the feed's: "G" goal, "SSG" saved by the goalkeeper, "SSP" saved by a player (a blocked shot, placed where it was taken) and "SPG" past the goal (missed the net). The feed times goals only, so the other shots have their period but no clock.

iihf.com itself refuses scripted requests; iihf_schedule() reads the same pages from its mirror at canada-central.iihf.com.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
# The 2026 Olympic final: Jack Hughes in overtime.
shots <- iihf_shots(1010000058)
shots[shots$result == "goal", c("period", "time", "team", "player_name", "x", "y", "distance")]
plot_shots(shots)
iihf_events(1010000058)

# The 2026 World Championship, and every shot of its opening game:
games <- iihf_schedule(2026, "wm")
iihf_shots(games$game_id[1])

# Every game of the 2026 Olympics:
iihf_olympic_games()
}
